name: Pneumococcal vaccine
protects_against: Pneumococcal disease, including pneumonia, meningitis and bloodstream infections

indications.reason: Adults aged 50 and older who haven't had a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine are recommended one dose.
indications.section: Pneumococcal vaccination: Routine vaccination (age 50 years or older)

indications.reason: Adults aged 19 to 49 with certain conditions are recommended pneumococcal vaccination. You reported one of these conditions.
indications.section: Pneumococcal vaccination: Special situations (age 19–49 years with risk conditions)

not_indicated_reason: Pneumococcal vaccination is routine from age 50, or earlier for people with certain health conditions. You didn't report any of those conditions.

series.note: One dose of PCV20 or PCV21 completes vaccination. If you get PCV15, a PPSV23 dose follows later. If you've had other pneumococcal vaccines, the next step depends on which ones.

contraindications.text: A severe allergic reaction (such as anaphylaxis) after a previous dose, or to a vaccine ingredient.

precautions.text: A moderate or severe illness right now, with or without fever.

content.disease: Pneumococcal bacteria can cause pneumonia (lung infection), ear and sinus infections, meningitis (infection of the covering of the brain and spinal cord), and bloodstream infections.
content.why: The risk of serious pneumococcal disease is higher from age 50 and for people with certain long-term conditions.
content.who: All adults aged 50 and older, and adults aged 19 to 49 with certain conditions (such as chronic heart, lung, liver or kidney disease, diabetes, smoking, a weakened immune system, or no working spleen).
content.doses_text: Usually one dose of PCV20 or PCV21.
content.catch_up: If you've had older pneumococcal vaccines (PCV13 or PPSV23), a professional can tell you whether you need another dose.
common_reactions: Redness, swelling, pain or tenderness where the shot was given
serious_reactions: A severe allergic reaction is very rare.
